Is there a rule in this sub against doing peoples' homework for them?

I can't see one. Sometimes lower level problems help mix it up in contrast to the technically in depth articles which apply to ~15% of programmers and 10% of programmers understand (looking at you RUST). A lower level problem, or particularly a fun mid level problem can help bring more programmers together.

Though yes, it is annoying seeing other people's homework, they don't benefit from having others do their homework, and sometimes I enjoy seeing unique problems, I hate see the giant problem lists that float around. In the mean time, their incompetence (from not doing their homework) makes the rest of us look better on the market, so it's not helping them, and it's not hurting us.

Hi v/trees I'm currently beta testing some new features for the Firefly 2, as I'm friends with the founders of the company. They're working on a new feature which should be out soon called Power Tuning which lets you control the vapor production of the device using an iPhone app.

Essentially what it does is allow you to change the power tuning anywhere between 89% and 111%. This changes the overall vapor production of a hit when inhaling. For example, I find a lower percentage such as 89% to be a bit more similar to the Firefly 1, and seems to reduce the overall vapor production for a lighter more flavorful hit with a wider taste profile. Where as 111% increased the vapor production significantly, and was more similar to taking a hit from a Pax 2 but lacked some of the finer notes flavor wise compared to the lowest power tuning setting even at the same heat profile.

Keep in mind, this is a variable setting in addition to the existing heating profiles. So you can power tune any of the existing heating profiles to get extra control over vapor production at any temperature.

It is a pretty interesting feature that should be out soon. I could see this coming in handy for power smokers who want bigger hits, as well as people new to smoking looking for a lighter less powerful hit for their first time.

I smoke medically, and sometimes I'm just looking for a light hit of CBD, or I'm just looking to take the edge off.
